questions.stem: A clinician's note graph has a vertical asymptote at x=2; what discontinuity?

options.text: Jump discontinuity due to finite jump
Infinite discontinuity due to unbounded growth

options.misconception: names "No discontinuity because asymptote" where the rule requires "Infinite discontinuity due to unbounded growth"

questions.explanation: The removable and infinite discontinuities principle here is: Asymptote means infinite. On that basis "Infinite discontinuity due to unbounded growth" is correct, while "Jump discontinuity due to finite jump" treats unbounded as finite jump.

questions.topic: The derivative from its limit definition
questions.stem: In a clinician's note f(x)=7 constant; by limit definition, f'(x) is?

options.misconception: confuses "Undefined because constant" with the correct "f'(x)=0 because derivative of constant is 0"

options.text: f'(x)=0 because derivative of constant is 0

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this the derivative from its limit definition item is: Constant rate of change is zero. That is why "f'(x)=0 because derivative of constant is 0" is right. The option "Undefined because constant" (confuses "Undefined because constant" with the correct "f'(x)=0 because derivative of constant is 0") does not satisfy the rule.
questions.hint: Constant rate of change is zero.

questions.stem: A clinician's note asks derivative of 5/(x+2); write model answer.

answer.exemplar: Using quotient rule with u=5, v=x+2 gives (0*(x+2)-5*1)/(x+2)^2 = -5/(x+2)^2.

options.text: Right-hand limit is 1 because floor near 1+ is 1
Right-hand limit is 2 because next integer

options.misconception: confuses jump with no one-sided limit

questions.explanation: Applying the one-sided limits rule — Evaluate just right of 1 — yields "Right-hand limit is 1 because floor near 1+ is 1". The tempting "Right-hand limit is 0 because floor(1)=0?" fails because it selects "Right-hand limit is 0 because floor(1)=0?" instead of "Right-hand limit is 1 because floor near 1+ is 1".
